question: Comparing the unilateral (1 tail) and bilateral hypothesis tests (2 tails):

options.opa: Bilateral tests always give higher p values.
options.opb: Bilateral tests always give lower p values.
options.opc: If a unilateral test is significant, so will the bilateral test.
options.opd: A bilateral test is more sensitive than a unilateral test.

analysis: In hypothesis testing, a bilateral (two-tailed) test considers both directions of an effect, while a unilateral (one-tailed) test considers only one direction. This means that the critical region for a two-tailed test is split between both tails of the distribution, making it harder to achieve significance compared to a one-tailed test. Therefore, bilateral tests generally result in higher p-values than unilateral tests when testing the same hypothesis. If a unilateral test is significant, it does not guarantee that the bilateral test will also be significant, as the latter requires a more extreme test statistic to reach significance. A bilateral test is not more sensitive than a unilateral test; in fact, it is less sensitive because it requires a more extreme result to reject the null hypothesis.
